doc.title: Bill Holman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 13, 1999

title: Electric instruments in big bands
summary: His band avoids electric instruments; Brookmeyer uses synthesizers.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: In your own band, I’m not sure how to ask this question, has electronics entered into, even in the big band field. Actually what I think I’m getting at is does your rhythm section use electric instruments and if so does it change the sound?

No we don’t use them. We use an amp on the bass, but that’s — no, in the jazz world there hasn’t been a whole lot of that, in the straight ahead jazz, the mainstream. Brookmeyer has used synthesizers to really good effect on some of the things that he’s done in Europe. But mostly for a straight ahead jazz band, an electric sound doesn’t fit. It doesn’t have that grease that you like to say that humans have.
